subject.declared_domain: The BINDING map from the archetype layer down to concrete substrate: role -> [node_type]. It is the only declared join between the 14-role vocabulary and the 58 node_types the derive runner actually emits, and it is what makes a role-keyed view of the estate possible at all.

methodology.how: A hand-legislated YAML block, top-level key `node_bindings:` at line 219. Twelve buckets, each a LIST of node_type strings: ten are role names, and two are NOT roles at all -- `contextual` and `scope_out`. A consumer inverts the map (node_type -> role) to classify. Nothing computes it; it changes by ratification plus a meta.version bump. It names 59 node_types across the 12 buckets.
declared_opinions: The bucket set MIXES TWO AXES. Ten buckets are ROLES; `contextual` and `scope_out` are HANDLING POLICIES. A consumer inverting the map gets 'Store' and 'scope_out' as peers, and only prose distinguishes them. That is CLAUDE.md Rule 24(iii) -- one axis serving two intents -- inside the map the whole archetype layer joins through.

WHICH node_type lands in WHICH bucket is a judgement with no stated derivation: Field and Prop are bound to Store; JSXRender and JSXElement to Sink; LAMBDA, Service, Component and ReactComponent to `contextual` rather than to any role.
The 4 roles with NO bucket (Custodian, Producer, Router, Source) are an omission the block does not mark. Nothing in the map says 'these four are deliberately unbound' -- their absence is silent.
`scope_out` (Type, Symbol, Concept) is a declared exclusion and is the block's most honest opinion: it refuses to force a role rather than inventing one.

composes.note: the role vocabulary this map binds down from; 10 of its 14 members appear as buckets

coverage.denominator: The block names 59 node_types across 12 buckets. Against the live graph at snapshot 2902399899597701830: 48 of 58 live node_types are bound (20,750 of 27,035 nodes, 76.8%); 10 of 58 live types are unbound (6,285 nodes, 23.2%). In the other direction, 11 of the 59 named types are DECLARED BUT NOT LIVE. Role side: 10 of 14 roles have a bucket.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: The block is passive data; its failure surfaces at the LOADER. All 8 loaders use the same shape -- yaml.safe_load then a dict lookup. On a miss the lookup returns None, silently. A member that does not exist and a live estate object this block has not covered both yield the same None.
silent_degrade_paths: the stale v1.1 copy carries the IDENTICAL `ratified: LD-0311 @086238604` string as the canonical while `meta.version` reads 1.1 -- a reader checking provenance gets an authoritative-looking answer from a seven-version-stale file. RATIFICATION IDENTITY DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE VINTAGE.
the block has no cadence, so it can fall behind a nightly-moving estate indefinitely with nothing signalling the gap

inverting the map yields 'scope_out' and 'contextual' as if they were roles; a consumer that does not special-case them silently classifies nodes into a handling policy

verdict.why: All seven rows worked with basis/evidence/owner and basis_by_field; not INCOMPLETE. The block does its job -- it is the only declared role-to-substrate bridge and it reaches 76.8% of live nodes -- and is QUALIFIED on four measured limits: (1) PARTIAL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, 48 of 58 live types bound and 11 of 59 named types not live, and neither figure substitutes for the other; (2) 4 of 14 roles have no bucket at all and their absence is unmarked; (3) the bucket set MIXES roles with handling policies (`contextual`, `scope_out`), so an inverted map presents them as peers and only prose separates them; (4) a miss returns a silent None, exercised. NOT CLAIMED: that any binding is CORRECT -- whether Field belongs under Store is a judgement recorded as a declared opinion, not adjudicated. NO DEPRECATION VERDICT, per W2-m-3.
